comparison_structure: Community-year strata with low/high OEND implementation versus no implementation
reported_mortality_result: ARR 0.73 (95% CI 0.57-0.91) for 1-100 enrollments/100k; ARR 0.54 (0.39-0.76) for >100 enrollments/100k
exclusion_reason: Poisson model adjusts for measured community-level covariates and AR(1) covariance but does not include community fixed effects

comparison_structure: Single national series; outcome is the share of opioid-related deaths occurring within 4 weeks of prison release
reported_mortality_result: Share fell from 9.8% to 6.3%: 36% relative reduction (95% CI 20-51%); absolute reduction 3.5 percentage points (1.6-5.4)
exclusion_reason: Uncontrolled pre-post with no comparison jurisdiction; outcome is a proportion of deaths rather than a death rate

design: One-group pre-post with county comparison; 38 North Carolina counties
comparison_structure: County-years grouped by cumulative kits distributed per 100k (0; 1-100; >100)
exclusion_reason: Log Poisson GEE with AR(1) working correlation and secular-trend adjustment; no county fixed effects (same structure as Walley 2013)

design: Hierarchical Bayesian spatiotemporal Poisson; 3,109 US counties
comparison_structure: States by Good Samaritan law type with and without an NAL; county conditional-autoregressive random effects
reported_mortality_result: GSL with arrest protection plus NAL, 2 years post-enactment: RR 0.90 (95% CrI 0.85-0.95) opioid deaths; 0.89 (0.82-0.96) heroin/synthetic; 0.93 (0.89-0.97) all overdose
exclusion_reason: NAL effect is estimated jointly with Good Samaritan law type and is not separately identified; county random rather than fixed effects

design: Interrupted time series; Ontario provincial series
comparison_structure: Single provincial series before and after the June 2016 Ontario Naloxone Program for Pharmacies; heterogeneity by public-health-unit implementation tertile
reported_mortality_result: Parsimonious level change RR 0.91 (95% CI 0.79-1.06); adjusted level RR 1.06 (0.94-1.19) and slope RR 1.06 (1.02-1.10); lowest-implementation tertile RR 0.75 (0.62-0.91)
exclusion_reason: One-group ITS with no untreated comparison jurisdiction

design: Linear panel regression; 3-digit ZIP by quarter in Massachusetts, Rhode Island, and New York City
comparison_structure: Continuous pharmacy and community naloxone per 100k, entered as same-quarter levels and quarter-to-quarter changes
reported_mortality_result: Same-quarter level: pharmacy +0.0071 (95% CI 0.0008-0.0133) and community +0.0047 (0.0016-0.0079) deaths per 100k per kit per 100k; changes -0.0049 (-0.0125 to 0.0026) and -0.0003 (-0.0037 to 0.0031)
exclusion_reason: ZIP fixed effects and a linear trend are present, but the authors interpret the positive level association as naloxone reaching high-mortality areas rather than a causal effect

design: Interrupted time series; Maryland statewide series
comparison_structure: Single statewide series before and after the 2017 expanded naloxone standing order
reported_mortality_result: Reported declines of 0.25 prescription-opioid deaths/100k, 1.83 heroin deaths/100k, and 2.54 fentanyl deaths/100k (abstract only; whether these are level or slope changes and the time unit are not stated)
exclusion_reason: One-group ITS has no untreated comparison jurisdiction and no unit fixed effects; cannot separate policy change from coincident statewide shocks

design: ARIMA interrupted time series; Clark County, Nevada
comparison_structure: Single county series before and after naloxone dispensing from public health vending machines (March 2019)
reported_mortality_result: Step change -8.52 opioid-involved deaths per month (p = 0.002); slope change +1.01 per month (p < 0.001); 41 deaths averted in the first 12 months (229 observed versus 270 forecast)

comparison_structure: State-years with versus without an NAL; random state intercept and quadratic time trajectory
exclusion_reason: Random intercept rather than state fixed effects; no event-study or pre-trend check

design: Interrupted time series; Alberta municipalities and province
comparison_structure: Municipal and provincial series before and after the community-based naloxone program (January 2016) and supervised consumption sites (2018)
reported_mortality_result: Urban opioid-related deaths level change +9.1 per month (+40%; 95% CI 6.7 to 11.5) after the naloxone program
exclusion_reason: One-group ITS; the naloxone interruption coincides with fentanyl emergence in Alberta

design: Interrupted time series; state-level opioid deaths ages 15-24
comparison_structure: States grouped by type of naloxone access law
reported_mortality_result: Trend (slope) IRR 0.97 (0.91-1.04) for patient-specific laws and 1.01 (0.96-1.06) for patient-nonspecific laws; immediate level-change IRR 0.88 (0.50-1.25) and 1.10 (0.94-1.27)
exclusion_reason: Published methods use population-averaged negative-binomial models; no state fixed effects reported

design: Multisite interrupted time series; 351 Massachusetts municipalities
reported_mortality_result: Annualized RR 0.84 (0.78-0.91) for postimplementation slope; adjusted level change RR 1.09 (0.99-1.20)
exclusion_reason: Segmented Poisson GEE adjusts for measured municipal covariates but does not include municipality fixed effects

design: Before-after with historic control period; Skane County, Sweden
comparison_structure: Single region; take-home naloxone intervention period compared with a historic control period
reported_mortality_result: Overdose deaths fell from 3.9 to 2.8 per 100k; IRR 0.72 (95% CI 0.56-0.92); men 0.65 (0.49-0.85); women 1.07 (0.60-1.87)

design: Controlled interrupted time series; three Eastern Missouri regional series
comparison_structure: St. Louis City, St. Louis County, and collar-county trajectories compared using ARIMA/CITS
reported_mortality_result: St. Louis City immediate level change -2.17 opioid-overdose deaths/100k/month (95% CI -3.28 to -1.06) and post-naloxone slope change -0.28/month (-0.37 to -0.18)
exclusion_reason: Controlled ITS over three aggregate units; region indicators act as unit effects, but identification rests on two comparison series rather than a panel

design: Community-level cohort within the HEALing Communities Study; 67 communities by quarter
comparison_structure: Naloxone distributed in the prior 12 months, in tertiles (<=1,000; 1,001-3,000; >3,000 units per 100k)
exclusion_reason: Linear mixed model with community random intercepts and slopes; observational exposure nested in the trial

design: Segmented Poisson interrupted time series; Galveston County, Texas census tracts
comparison_structure: Single county series before and after hotspot-targeted naloxone distribution
exclusion_reason: Uncontrolled ITS; preprint; overlaps the national 2023-2025 decline in overdose deaths
